Heteromorph Health Care.text: Heteromorph health care is ordinary medicine adjusted to bodies that follow their own rules, and its quality depends on where a patient lives. Large hospitals keep Quirk specialists who can read an unusual heartbeat, set a bone in a wing, treat scales or fur and size a dose for a body far heavier, lighter or differently built than the textbook patient. Smaller clinics often lack the equipment: a blood-pressure cuff that does not fit, a scanner too narrow, a dentist with no plan for a beak or tusks. Many heteromorph families carry a file on their own body to every appointment. Public insurance covers specialist care, though rural patients may travel far for it. Sending a heteromorph patient to a veterinarian, or joking about it, is an insult that makes the news.
